tools.name: search_hoteli
tools.description: Search for Hoteli on the Hotels search form.  Builds the search and moves the user to the results page - it does not return offers or prices itself; read those from the results page.

place.description: Exactly one destination or specific hotel name as the user said it, e.g. "Crete" or "Blue Lagoon Resort".

exactDates.description: The fixed hotel stay dates. Hotel search does not support flexible date windows.

checkin.description: Check-in date in ISO YYYY-MM-DD format.

checkout.description: Check-out date in ISO YYYY-MM-DD format.

rooms.description: Defaults to one room, two adults, when omitted.

childrenAges.description: Each child's age. Every child needs an age - do not call with a missing one.

tools.name: search_let_hotel
tools.description: Search for Let+Hotel on the Portfolio search form.  Builds the search and moves the user to the results page - it does not return offers or prices itself; read those from the results page.

destinations.description: Destination names as the user said them, e.g. ["Crete", "Rhodes"]. Omit or send an empty list when the user wants any destination.

departures.description: Departure city/airport names as the user said them. Omit for no departure restriction.

exactDates.description: Use ONLY when the user knows the real travel dates, e.g. "out on 12 June, back on the 19th". The form may represent this as two calendar dates or as a departure date plus the derived stay length. Never use this to express a period to search inside - for that use searchWindow.

outbound.description: ISO YYYY-MM-DD. The day the traveller actually flies out.

inbound.description: ISO YYYY-MM-DD. The day they actually fly back. On departure-date forms this is used to derive the stay length. Omit if only the outbound day is fixed - then give nights.

searchWindow.description: Use whenever the user described a PERIOD rather than dates: "sometime in November", "all of November", "the first two weeks of July", "anytime this summer". These are the bounds of the period to search inside, NOT the trip itself - the trip is shorter and floats within them. Always pair with nights. If the user gave any period at all, send it here - do not drop the dates because they are not exact.

from.description: ISO YYYY-MM-DD. Earliest day the trip may start.

to.description: ISO YYYY-MM-DD. Latest day the trip may end.

nights.description: How many nights the trip lasts ("5 nights" = 5, "a week" = 7, "a fortnight" = 14). Required with searchWindow. Never derive it from the length of searchWindow - a one-month window is not a one-month trip. With exactDates it may replace an omitted inbound date; when both are supplied, the explicit nights value controls stay-length selectors.

nightsMax.description: Upper bound when the user gave a range of nights, e.g. nights: 7, nightsMax: 10 for "1-1.5 weeks".

rooms.description: Defaults to one room, two adults, when omitted.

childrenAges.description: Each child's age. Every child needs an age - do not call with a missing one.
